layers.note: A cushion herb of dry subalpine and alpine slopes, pumice and rock.

elevation_m.note: Montane to alpine; about 1,200 m and up in Washington.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −18 to 0 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 4 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 7 to 18 °C; gone below 4 °C, where summers are too short, and above 22 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 600 to 3,200 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: About 150 to 1,700 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 60.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.3, gone by 0.15.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Spreading phlox grows from British Columbia to California and east to Montana (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
